mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS changes (p > 0.05) in the identified regime, or the rate stays below 4% for the required window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points in the same
failure_condition: In the specified regime, the correlation between PAYEMS change and SPX 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05), or the return direction is opposite to the predicted one.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 3% suggests expanding economic demand, which anticipates stronger corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Over the 5-day horizon, SPX 20-day forward returns do not outperform a baseline of zero (no signal) with a Z-score > 1.65, indicating the signal failed to predict direction.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 1% over two months indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain higher rates and suppressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by >1% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative relative to CPIAUCSL changes (p > 0.05) in the identified regime.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of RSAFS to GDP (as approximated by GDPC1) falls below 0.8 for three consecutive months, it indicates a weakening demand environment that reduces growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS / GDPC1 < 0.8 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In the regime, the 60-day forward return is not significantly different from the mean of the prior 12 months (p > 0.05) when the trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% triggers a strong labor market interpretation that, if sustained, increases investor optimism and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% and remains below for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically positive when UNRATE is below 4% (p > 0.05), or the effect reverses in subsequent months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) for four consecutive months below 2% suggests the Fed is likely to hold rates steady, reducing discount rate expectations and supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not higher than the 5-day average of the prior 12 months when CPIAUCSL is in deflationary trend.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) both show double-digit monthly growth simultaneously, it indicates a resilient supply-side expansion that boosts growth expectations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by >10% and HOUST increases by >10% in the same month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically positive when both proxies meet the trigger (p > 0.05), or the effect is reversed in subsequent months.
